result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B takes a firmer position, names more of what already works (the single color, the black receipt version, use across sign, bag and receipt), and says plainly what evidence would justify a rebrand. However, B's 'build out the system' section (graphic devices, type and color roles, several lockups) goes beyond small refinements. A is a bit leaner, but it hedges with 'mostly keep it' and suggests a separate sans-serif for digital, which would split the identity. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A takes a firmer keep-and-refine position. It names more of what already works, including the single color and the black receipt version, and it explains clearly why a gradient would not help. A loses some credit for expanding into a wider system with a graphic device, layout rules and a symbol-only lockup. B hedges with 'mostly keep', leaves out the black version, and suggests a sans-serif for digital use, which starts to split the identity, but it gives good tests of whether a rebrand is really justified.
